newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says N. Korea keeping nuclear agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says N. Korea keeping nuclear agreement.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday North Korea was living up to several parts of an agreement under which it will transform its nuclear programme to exclusively peaceful uses.
In a memorandum for Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, Clinton said Washington was taking steps to assure that progress was being made on the 1992 agreement.
He said the North Koreans were cooperating fully in the canning and safe storage of all spent fuel from its graphite-moderated nuclear reactors with such canning due to be completed later this year.
Clinton also said North Korea had not significantly diverted U.S. assistance for purposes other than for which it was intended.
Under the agreement, Washington promised the isolationist state two light-water reactors if Pyongyang froze and ultimately dismantled its existing nuclear programme.
North Korea was assured interim energy in the form of 500,000 metric tons of heavy fuel oil per year for heating and electricity.
Light-water reactors are less suitable for producing weapons-grade plutonium.
